subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Allen Stanford's Cricket Ponzi
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Allen Stanford's Cricket Ponzi.

hook.text: Allen Stanford used a bank in Antigua to sell fake CDs with impossible returns. He spent the money on cricket.

buildup.text: Stanford Financial Group sold $7 billion in certificates of deposit with above-market interest rates.

discovery.text: The CDs weren't real investments. Stanford used new money to pay old investors and fund his lavish lifestyle.

twist.text: Stanford sponsored cricket tournaments to build legitimacy. His name was on stadiums across the Caribbean.

climax.text: Stanford got 110 years in prison. The SEC had received tips about him for years before acting.

punchline.text: $7 billion in fake CDs. Cricket sponsorships. 110 years in prison.

quiz.question: Where was Allen Stanford's fraudulent bank based?
